what_changed.headline: Energy shock is driving a renewed inflation-and-rates repricing
what_changed.significance: ECB projections raised medium-term inflation while conflict-related energy disruption remains the main upside risk; the ECB also described stronger near-term growth than previously expected.
what_changed.transmission: Higher oil and gas prices lift headline inflation and inflation persistence, increasing tightening risk while weakening rate-sensitive demand.

what_changed.headline: US and UK policy paths are increasingly divergent in interpretation
what_changed.significance: ING expects a one-off 25bp Fed hike, while it expects the BoE to remain on hold; supplied research disagrees on the BoE’s near-term risk.
what_changed.transmission: A Fed hike may support the dollar and front-end yields, while a BoE hold would limit sterling support despite higher energy inflation.

executive_decisions.development: Treat energy persistence—not the initial price shock—as the key policy variable.
executive_decisions.why_it_matters: A sustained shock could generate second-round inflation and prolong restrictive policy; a reversal would challenge current hawkish forecasts.
executive_decisions.transmission: Monitor energy flows, fuel pass-through, wages and services pricing before extending duration or adding rate exposure.

executive_decisions.development: Keep duration exposure tactical and conditional.
executive_decisions.why_it_matters: European rates have sold off sharply, but sources cite uncertainty around energy, global-rate beta and technical positioning.
executive_decisions.transmission: Stabilising energy prices and softer inflation would support duration; persistent energy pressure would extend the sell-off.

macro_themes.theme: Energy supply shock becomes a policy shock
macro_themes.thesis: The macro consequence depends on persistence and pass-through, not merely the initial rise in energy prices.
macro_themes.market_implication: Near-term bias remains toward higher inflation risk, tighter policy expectations and pressure on duration; growth-sensitive assets remain vulnerable if the shock persists.

observed_facts.text: ECB baseline projections show euro-area inflation above target through 2027, while its adverse scenarios show materially higher inflation and weaker growth.

inferences.text: Persistent energy disruption creates a stagflationary policy dilemma and raises the hurdle for duration longs.

conflicting_evidence.text: ING argues that limited wage and services pass-through could prevent a durable second-round inflation process in the UK.

unresolved_questions: Do energy flows normalise before wage and services-price resets?
Will central banks look through the shock or respond to persistence?

transmission.implication: Upside inflation risk supports higher front-end and intermediate yields until energy or inflation data turn.
Energy remains supported by physical disruption; industrial metals face growth and yield headwinds.
Higher US rates may support USD; JPY resilience depends on BoJ communication.
Energy equities may hedge, while rate-sensitive and cyclical sectors face pressure.

catalysts: US inflation and the Fed decision
Evidence on Strait of Hormuz shipping
invalidation_conditions: Clear deterioration in activity without persistent inflation

macro_themes.theme: AI investment supports activity but raises capital-intensity and valuation questions
macro_themes.thesis: AI demand is observable, but the market outcome depends on conversion into cash flow and durable pricing power.
macro_themes.market_implication: Infrastructure beneficiaries may remain supported, while software and credit exposures require proof of monetisation.

observed_facts.text: Oracle reported 121% cloud-infrastructure revenue growth and substantial data-centre capital expenditure, according to Saxo’s earnings summary.
ECB analysis reports stronger financing growth for AI-related firms than for the rest of the economy.

inferences.text: AI investment can support growth while also sustaining demand for capital and keeping long rates structurally sensitive.

unresolved_questions: Will infrastructure revenue convert into free cash flow?
Will AI improve software pricing power or accelerate substitution?

transmission.implication: Hardware and infrastructure beneficiaries may outperform software if monetisation remains stronger in compute than applications.
Large AI-related issuance could pressure spreads if supply rises faster than absorption.
Persistent capital expenditure can support higher real-rate and term-premium risks.

catalysts: Evidence on AI financing and cash-flow conversion

asset_views.transmission: A BoJ hike supports the yen through higher domestic rates; disappointment would widen the relative-rate gap against JPY.

risks: BoJ fails to validate faster tightening.

counterevidence.text: ING warns that yen bulls could be disappointed if follow-up tightening is not endorsed.

candidate_expressions.thesis: Energy persistence keeps euro-area front-end rate risk skewed higher, but the trade should be conditional on market confirmation.
candidate_expressions.expression: Conditional pay-fixed exposure in 2-year EUR swaps, or a payer option on 2-year EUR rates.
candidate_expressions.why_now: ECB projections and energy disruption have raised the policy-risk premium, while the next inflation and energy signals can quickly reverse the move.
candidate_expressions.catalyst: Upside euro-area inflation surprise or evidence that energy disruption persists.
candidate_expressions.expected_path: Higher front-end rates initially, with a possible reversal if energy flows normalise and underlying inflation remains contained.
candidate_expressions.invalidation_condition: Sustained energy-price reversal accompanied by softer core inflation and wages.
candidate_expressions.countercase: The shock remains supply-driven and central banks look through it, allowing rates to retrace.
implementation_risks: Gap risk around policy and inflation events.
High volatility and uncertain energy path.
Market confirmation is required; no independent live market-data feed is supplied.
candidate_expressions.alternative_expression: Relative-value short EUR front-end versus long US front-end, subject to verified rate and basis data.
candidate_expressions.evidence_quality: Strong primary ECB evidence, supplemented by attributed bank analysis; no independent market confirmation.
candidate_expressions.confidence_rationale: Code-calibrated evidence strength: 3 cited document(s) from 3 conservatively independent evidence family/families from 3 publisher(s); strongest tier is primary. Explicit counterevidence reduces the displayed tier. Expression confidence is capped at 2/5 without market data.

signposts: Energy flows remain disrupted but improve intermittently.

ECB and Fed retain optionality rather than signal an extended cycle.

assumptions.text: ECB baseline projections remain broadly relevant unless energy disruption worsens.

themes.title: Energy supply shock becomes a policy shock
themes.implication: Near-term bias remains toward higher inflation risk, tighter policy expectations and pressure on duration; growth-sensitive assets remain vulnerable if the shock persists.

themes.title: AI investment supports activity but raises capital-intensity and valuation questions
themes.implication: Infrastructure beneficiaries may remain supported, while software and credit exposures require proof of monetisation.

themes.title: Energy shock meets restrictive policy
themes.implication: Policy rates can remain high even as growth weakens, increasing duration and cyclical-equity sensitivity.

themes.title: Long-end yield pressure is becoming a cross-asset constraint
themes.implication: Duration, credit and rate-sensitive equities remain vulnerable if yields continue higher.

themes.title: Energy shock versus disinflation
themes.implication: Prefer monitoring inflation-sensitive rates and margins over assuming a broad inflation spiral.

themes.title: AI investment cycle: strong demand, uncertain monetisation
themes.implication: The cycle supports semiconductors and selected infrastructure, while financing needs and model-price competition create credit and equity dispersion.

themes.title: Energy shock versus growth
themes.implication: Near-term inflation pressure favors caution on duration; growth deterioration would reverse that bias.

themes.title: Yen normalization and carry risk
themes.implication: Maintain vigilance on carry-sensitive exposures; continuation requires policy and flow support.

themes.title: Supply-driven inflation versus resilient demand
themes.implication: Rates risk remains asymmetric to the upside in the near term, while growth-sensitive assets face margin and real-income pressure.

themes.title: AI investment moves from capability to economics
themes.implication: AI exposure remains differentiated: infrastructure demand is supported, while cash generation, utilization and software defensibility become decisive.

themes.title: Energy scarcity is extending inflation and policy risk
themes.implication: Higher energy volatility can delay monetary easing, pressure rate-sensitive assets and support energy-linked commodities.

themes.title: Monetary-policy divergence is being tested by data
themes.implication: Front-end rates, the dollar and risk assets remain highly sensitive to CPI and central-bank decisions.

themes.title: Sovereign supply and market intermediation
themes.implication: Long-duration rates may remain vulnerable even if near-term policy expectations soften; liquidity conditions should be monitored rather than assumed benign.

themes.title: Fiscal and supply pressure at the long end
themes.implication: Long-end rates remain vulnerable, with knock-on pressure for property, small caps and speculative growth.

themes.title: AI investment remains structurally supported but increasingly selective
themes.implication: Prefer profitable cash generators and energy infrastructure over unprofitable, financing-dependent growth; market confirmation is unavailable.

themes.title: Supply-driven inflation versus restrictive policy
themes.implication: The combination can keep rates higher for longer while weakening real household income and cyclical demand.

themes.title: Global yield and fiscal-risk repricing
themes.implication: The shock is negative for duration and broad risk appetite, but its FX effect is ambiguous where higher yields are interpreted as fiscal rather than monetary strength.

themes.title: AI adoption is broadening, but near-term labour displacement remains limited
themes.implication: The evidence supports gradual labour transformation rather than an immediate employment shock, while investment exposure is more credible through infrastructure and productivity channels than through an assumed aggregate-demand boom.

themes.title: AI investment is becoming a cross-market financing and duration shock
themes.implication: Favourable AI demand does not eliminate financing risk: supply, concentration, leverage and delayed revenue realization can raise credit premia and pressure long-duration assets.
